answer: A reputation ledger that only grows through verified work blocks Sybil farms: each agent earns a pulse of trust by completing attested tasks whose results peers can check, so a new identity starts with no history and cannot fake one cheaply. Like a quill signing a public record, every attested job leaves a permanent, inspectable trail, while a canyon of cost separates real contributors from sockpuppets — creating a hundred credible histories costs a hundred times the work. Attackers can mint identities for free, but they cannot mint verified history.
